title: Chimera II OS Universal ISA Database
accuracy_note: value_bits is a canonical encoding or fixed-bit pattern; mask_bits marks fixed bits. Zero mask bits are operand-variable fields. Chimera-native encodings are project-defined. The current instruction rows are a partial catalog of verified forms, not an exhaustive enumeration of every instruction, extension, CPU model, or encoding variant. A target is compiler-supported only for forms implemented by the encoder/decoder and backend; catalog presence alone does not imply complete executable support. Internet research update 2026-10-08: additions are sourced from the official ISA specifications listed in sources; this remains a partial catalog and each encoding must be verified against the referenced architecture manual before use in an executable encoder/decoder. Inventory update 2026-10-09: added a broad architecture-family inventory covering historical, current, embedded, vector, GPU, and virtual ISAs. Rows marked catalog-only are discovery targets and have zero verified instruction forms; the inventory is intentionally not represented as literally exhaustive, and does not imply encoder, decoder, simulator, or hardware support. GPU/VM/extension entries are explicitly distinguished from general-purpose CPU base ISAs.

research_update.method: Official vendor and standards documentation reviewed for architecture scope, instruction reference organization, and extension/version status. Curated reference supplement; not exhaustive.

source_findings.finding: Intel SDM separates basic architecture, the full A–Z instruction reference, system programming (memory management, protection, interrupts/exceptions, multiprocessor, VMX/VT, SGX), and model-specific registers. Track extension and processor feature availability separately.
An ISA specifies programmer-visible instructions, formats, registers, data types, memory model, privilege, and exceptions; distinguish ISA from microarchitecture.

Track AArch64/A64 separately from AArch32 A32 and T32 (Thumb/Thumb-2); A64 is fixed 32-bit while T32 uses 16- and 32-bit encodings. Feature availability depends on architecture profile/version and implemented extensions.

RISC-V is modular: record base ISA, extensions, privileged architecture, and ratification status independently. Compressed C instructions use 16-bit encodings; base instructions commonly use 32 bits. The ratified library contains extensions beyond M/A/F/D/C/V.
Power ISA 3.1c defines user, virtual-environment, and operating-environment architecture in separate books; distinguish ISA instructions from platform requirements.

isa_inventory_policy.scope: Broad discoverable inventory of major CISC, RISC, EPIC/VLIW, GPU, virtual-machine and extension ISAs; not a claim that every proprietary, unpublished, historical, or custom ISA is enumerated.

status_semantics.standard: Existing architecture-level designation; verify version/profile applicability
status_semantics.legacy/standard: Legacy family with published architectural variants
status_semantics.catalog-only: Inventory/source target only; no instruction forms asserted
status_semantics.project-defined: Defined by Chimera II OS project

isa_inventory_policy.verification_rule: Instruction rows must be added only from a versioned authoritative reference or validated machine-readable definition. TableGen identifiers and family names are discovery candidates, not automatically architectural mnemonics or conformance evidence.
